messages.content: You check one debater against its own earlier words. You bring nothing from outside the words quoted to you: no doctrine, no training knowledge, no reading of your own. You do not judge who is right, and you do not judge the other side.

Each item gives one verse, the words a side wrote about it in its CLOSE round, and the words the SAME side wrote about it in its EARLIER rounds (R1 to R3).
Decide only this: does the close assert a reading of that verse, or of what it shows, that the same side's earlier words deny or contradict? A reading here is who did what to whom, what the verse forbids or allows, what it states or shows.
CONSISTENT: the close repeats, narrows, adds footing, answers the opponent, or keeps the earlier reading.
REVERSED: the close says the opposite of what the same side said before about the same verse, so that the earlier words and the close cannot both be the side's reading.
NO EARLIER READING: the earlier words name the verse but state no reading of it.
Quote exactly, copying the words as they stand in the item.
Reply with exactly one line per item id, and nothing else, in this form:
ANTICHEAT: <item id> -- CONSISTENT | REVERSED | NO EARLIER READING -- CLOSE: "<the close words that decide it>" -- EARLIER: "<the earlier words they keep or contradict>"

(answers C5)** / - [L4] Haggai 2:23 sets Zerubbabel as a signet. It says nothing of him sitting on the throne of David and ruling in Judah, which is what Jeremiah 22:30 withholds. I do not claim the sentence is broken. I claim only that a claim to the throne resting on Joseph's seed alone sits under Jeremiah 22:30. That is the footing of D4 as narrowed, and the unnamed premise in Luke 1:32 is the throne given "unto him."

[R3] - Haggai 2:23: "will make thee as a signet". Zerubbabel is called "my servant" and is not set on the throne. Jeremiah 22:24 is a sentence on Coniah and Jeremiah 22:30 bars his seed from the throne. Jeremiah 18:8 is conditional on a nation turning. Neither verse reverses the ban on Coniah's seed sitting on the throne.

[R2] - [L2] *zera'* (H2233, "seed, offspring") names the offspring of the cursed man.

[R2] - Link 4 stands on Jeremiah 22:30 with the Heli and Nathan rows.
[R1] [L1] Jeremiah 22:30: "Write ye this man childless... for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah."
[R1] [L2] In Jeremiah 22:30 the Hebrew *zera'* (H2233, "seed, offspring") names the descendants of the man being cursed. Joseph, in Matthew's chain, is of that seed.
[R1] [L4] The seed of Jechonias is barred from the throne (Jeremiah 22:30), and Joseph is in that seed (Matthew 1:11-12).
